portrays.reason: Anger takes your own smile and joy, which makes it an enemy like no other.
portrays.quote: Anger kills your smile and your joy

portrays.reason: If it isn’t guarded against, the one anger destroys is you.
portrays.quote: it is you that anger kills

portrays.reason: Anger doesn’t stop with you. It burns your own people, the raft that keeps you safe.
portrays.quote: burns the raft of safety that is your own people

portrays.reason: To value anger is to be hurt by it, as surely as a hand that strikes the ground.
portrays.quote: Someone who prizes anger will be ruined

portrays.reason: Anger taken far enough leaves a person no different from the dead.
portrays.quote: Those far gone in anger are like the dead

portrays.reason: Someone who can’t put anger down is easy for anyone to beat, anywhere, at any time.
portrays.quote: He doesn’t give up anger and has no self-command

portrays.reason: Anger that blinds makes a man the kind of enemy others are glad to have.
portrays.quote: A man of blinding anger

portrays.reason: A ruler who rages without thinking things through with his circle sees his good fortune shrink.
portrays.quote: flies into a rage, his good fortune shrinks

answers.reason: The real test is holding back where your anger could do damage, not where it can’t reach.
answers.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect

answers.reason: Says to keep anger out even of your thoughts, and that all you have set your mind on then comes.
answers.quote: never even think of anger in your heart

answers.reason: Holding back anger goes with learning and restraint here, and righteousness comes looking for such a person.
answers.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint

portrays.reason: The envious need no enemy. Envy by itself brings their ruin.
portrays.quote: Envy alone is enough for the envious

portrays.reason: Envy is called a sinner here, one that wrecks what you have and carries you somewhere worse.
portrays.quote: destroys your wealth and sends you to an evil place

portrays.reason: Refusing to be glad of another’s prosperity is the same as wanting no good of your own.
portrays.quote: Whoever envies another’s prosperity and won’t welcome it

portrays.reason: Grudging what others are given ends up costing your own people their food and clothes.
portrays.quote: Whoever grudges what others are given

portrays.reason: Good fortune can’t stay with the envious. She hands them to her elder sister and leaves.
portrays.quote: cannot bear the envious

portrays.reason: The sight of what others wear and eat sets the low to finding fault with them.
portrays.quote: they can always find a fault in them

answers.reason: Makes a heart free of envy a rule of conduct to be held to.
answers.quote: keep your heart free of envy

answers.reason: Being free of envy towards everyone is ranked with the greatest of blessings.
answers.quote: If you can be free of envy towards everyone

answers.reason: Knowing the harm of a bad path is what holds people back from acting on envy.
answers.quote: do nothing unrighteous out of envy

answers.reason: Envy has never raised anyone, and having none of it has never cost anyone their prosperity.
answers.quote: No one has grown great through envy

portrays.reason: Suffering clings to those who cling, and doesn’t let go of them.
portrays.quote: Suffering holds on and won’t let go

portrays.reason: Where craving is, suffering keeps coming, one after another, with no end.
portrays.quote: suffering comes on and on, without end

answers.reason: Says that each thing you let go of is one thing that can no longer cause you pain.
answers.quote: you suffer no more pain

answers.reason: Says the sorrow in the mind is hard to remove without reaching the feet of the one who has no equal.
answers.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

answers.reason: Promises no suffering, ever, to those who reach the feet of the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing.
answers.quote: will have no suffering, ever

answers.reason: Not craving pleasure, and calling suffering natural, is what keeps sorrow from coming.
answers.quote: says suffering is natural

answers.reason: Says to cherish and keep close the people who can end a suffering that has come.
answers.quote: those who can end the suffering that has come

portrays.reason: Craving is named as the seed of birth that never ends, for every living thing.
portrays.quote: craving is the seed that yields

portrays.reason: Craving works by deceiving you, so fearing it is called righteousness.
portrays.quote: Craving is what deceives you

portrays.reason: Craving is itself called the worst suffering, not just a cause of it.
portrays.quote: craving, the worst suffering of all

portrays.reason: However much it gets, craving stays unfilled, because that is its nature.
portrays.quote: whose nature is never to be filled

portrays.reason: Each loss makes gambling more loved, not less, and the soul goes the same way with pain.
portrays.quote: gambling is loved more with each loss

portrays.reason: He hears his heart’s hope of joining one who lets a sulk wither, and calls it what it is.
portrays.quote: That is only craving

answers.reason: Cutting craving off completely is the step named, and deeds that never fail you follow.
answers.quote: If you cut off craving completely

answers.reason: Giving up what can never be filled gives you, at that very moment, a nature that doesn’t change.
answers.quote: If you give up craving

answers.reason: The free are defined as those free of craving. No one else is free in the same way.
answers.quote: the ones free of craving

answers.reason: Having no craving is called purity, and it comes from wanting truthfulness.
answers.quote: Purity is having no craving

portrays.reason: What you hold on to is mirrored by what holds on to you. Suffering grips those who grip.
portrays.quote: those who hold on to attachment and won’t let go

portrays.reason: A single possession is enough to bring the old confusion back.
portrays.quote: Owning even one thing brings back delusion

portrays.reason: Those who haven’t let go completely are pictured as deluded and caught in a net.
portrays.quote: deluded, and caught in a net

answers.reason: Hold on to the one who holds on to nothing, as the way to let go of everything else.
answers.quote: so that you can let go of attachment

answers.reason: Letting go can go thing by thing, and each one let go stops being a source of pain.
answers.quote: From each thing you have let go of

answers.reason: Know what to rest on and live so that attachment dies, and the ills on their way to you won’t come.
answers.quote: live so that attachment dies

answers.reason: Not clinging at the moment of gain is what spares you the grief of loss.
answers.quote: never clung to what they gained

portrays.reason: She tells a friend who says women like her can cross it that desire is a real sea.
portrays.quote: There is indeed a sea of desire

portrays.reason: The joy of desire is a sea, and the pain when it turns on you is greater still.
portrays.quote: the pain is greater than that sea

portrays.reason: Desire sweeps away shame and strength together, the very raft that should carry you.
portrays.quote: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft

portrays.reason: Desire has no regard for how firm a person is or how much they deserve pity. It breaks out anyway.
portrays.quote: It breaks out of hiding into the open

portrays.reason: Gossip and a mother’s words only feed it, like manure and water on a plant.
portrays.quote: this sickness grows on

portrays.reason: Trying to shame desire away with gossip only feeds it, as ghee feeds a fire.
portrays.quote: put out a fire with ghee

portrays.reason: Fire burns when touched. Desire goes on burning when you have moved away from it.
portrays.quote: Can it burn when you leave it

portrays.reason: Desire can’t be kept hidden. It comes out unannounced, as a sneeze does.
portrays.quote: it comes out without warning, like a sneeze

portrays.reason: Desire is more tender than a flower, and few ever find it at its peak.
portrays.quote: Desire is softer than a flower

portrays.reason: Desire can intoxicate on a thought or a glance, which toddy can’t do.
portrays.quote: To be drunk at a thought and elated at a glance

portrays.reason: For this sickness the only medicine is the one who gave it.
portrays.quote: she herself is the medicine

portrays.reason: She tries to hide it, and it wells up the more, like water in a spring that is drawn from.
portrays.quote: it rises like spring water for those who draw it

portrays.reason: Caught both ways, she can’t hide it, and telling him would shame her.
portrays.quote: I can’t hide this sickness

portrays.reason: The long nights hurt her more than his cruelty does.
portrays.quote: these nights that now drag on

portrays.reason: Her heart can go to him and her eyes can’t, so they stay behind and swim in tears.
portrays.quote: swimming in this flood of water

portrays.reason: He is barely on his way when the pallor starts to spread over her.
portrays.quote: Look here, pallor spreading over my body

portrays.reason: Even a small shift in an embrace is enough to bring the pallor on, thick enough to scoop up.
portrays.quote: I lay holding him and shifted a little

portrays.reason: Evening brings it on. As the light turns pale, despair buds and pain grows.
portrays.quote: despair buds in me and pain grows

portrays.reason: With him away, each evening comes to her like strangers to a killing ground.
portrays.quote: evening comes like strangers to a killing ground

portrays.reason: Evening was only evening until he left.
portrays.quote: I never knew that evening brings pain

portrays.reason: The sickness keeps a daily round, growing from morning until it blooms at evening.
portrays.quote: buds in the morning, fills out all day and flowers in the evening

portrays.reason: Her friend sees his unkindness told in her eyes, pale and running with tears.
portrays.quote: pale and streaming with tears

portrays.reason: Her friend sees it in her body. Her arms waste and her bangles slide off.
portrays.quote: Now they shrink and the gold bangles slip away

portrays.reason: Union itself has turned painful, because now it holds the fear that he will leave.
portrays.quote: the pain of fearing he will leave

portrays.reason: If even those who understand can leave, no promise settles her fear.
portrays.quote: Even those who understand can sometimes leave

portrays.reason: He said “Don’t be afraid,” and now he is going. She asks if she is to blame for believing him.
portrays.quote: is there any fault in those who trusted what he swore

portrays.reason: Someone hard enough to say he is leaving leaves her little to hope for.
portrays.quote: there is little hope that he will be kind

portrays.reason: Living among strangers is painful, and parting from those dear to you is worse.
portrays.quote: More painful still is parting from those dear to you

portrays.reason: Even having him brings no rest. Her heart simply moves from one fear to the other.
portrays.quote: when it has him it fears parting

portrays.reason: She has counted off the days since he left until her fingers wore down.
portrays.quote: my fingers have worn down from touching off the days

portrays.reason: The thought of his return makes her heart climb like a plant putting out branches.
portrays.quote: my heart grows branches and climbs

portrays.reason: All she wants is to look at him until her eyes are full, and then the pallor will go.
portrays.quote: Let me see my husband until my eyes are full

portrays.reason: One day with him, she says, and she will drink until all this sickness is gone.
portrays.quote: Let my husband come, just one day

portrays.reason: She is so ready for him that she can’t decide what she will do first when he comes.
portrays.quote: shall I sulk, shall I embrace him

portrays.reason: He longs too, far off at the ruler’s work, for the win that will let him go home to her.
portrays.quote: give the evening a feast

portrays.reason: For those counting on a return, each day takes as long as seven.
portrays.quote: one day passes like seven

portrays.reason: He fears coming too late. If her heart breaks first, what use is it to have her?
portrays.quote: Once her heart has broken and spilled

portrays.reason: Her eyes’ wanting to see him feels like being eaten.
portrays.quote: Wanting to see him, they are eating me

portrays.reason: Like a load on one end of a carrying pole, desire on one side only is painful to bear.
portrays.quote: Desire on one side only is painful

portrays.reason: If he doesn’t love her too, there is nothing the one she loves can do for her.
portrays.quote: What can the one I love do for me

portrays.reason: She asks why the god of desire stays on one side only and doesn’t see her pain.
portrays.quote: The god of desire stays on one side only

portrays.reason: To her, those whose love is returned have the fruit without the stone.
portrays.quote: the stoneless fruit of desire

portrays.reason: Telling your pain to one who isn’t close to you would be like trying to fill in the sea.
portrays.quote: Fill in the sea instead

portrays.reason: He has shut her out of his heart, yet he keeps coming into hers.
portrays.quote: He has barred me from his heart

portrays.reason: She calls her own heart foolish for suffering over one with no love for her.
portrays.quote: He has no love for you, yet you go on suffering

portrays.reason: Why sit aching, she asks her heart, when the one who caused it has no tender thought for them?
portrays.quote: has no tender thought for us

portrays.reason: Her heart pines and still goes after the one who left, and she calls it a fool.
portrays.quote: You pine because he won’t show tender kindness

portrays.reason: Keeping in her heart one who left and won’t come near only costs her more.
portrays.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty

portrays.reason: He would say he remembers her, except that he has never learned to forget.
portrays.quote: I don’t know how to forget

portrays.reason: He is so present in her heart that she won’t eat anything hot, in case he burns.
portrays.quote: My lover lives in my heart

portrays.reason: Just thinking of desire brings a joy that doesn’t fade, which toddy can’t do.
portrays.quote: even thinking of it brings a great joy

portrays.reason: While he is thinking of the one he loves, there is no pain.
portrays.quote: When you think of the one you love, no pain comes

portrays.reason: She knows he is always in her heart and can only ask whether she is in his.
portrays.quote: In mine, oh, he is always there

portrays.reason: Forgetting is beyond her and remembering burns, so there is no easy place to stand.
portrays.quote: even remembering burns my heart

portrays.reason: The honour left to her is that he doesn’t object to how much she thinks of him.
portrays.quote: However much I think of him, he doesn’t get angry

portrays.reason: Asleep he is on her shoulders, awake he is in her heart. He doesn’t leave her either way.
portrays.quote: When I wake, he rushes into my heart

portrays.reason: A sneeze that fades makes her wonder if he nearly thought of her, and then didn’t.
portrays.quote: A sneeze starts to come and then dies away

portrays.reason: She sulks though he has done nothing wrong, because sulking brings out his tenderness.
portrays.quote: sulking is what draws out his tenderness

portrays.reason: The small hurt of a sulk dims his tenderness for a moment, and it comes back greater.
portrays.quote: but it comes back greater

portrays.reason: Even the pleasure of a sulk has its pain: what if coming together is delayed?
portrays.quote: There is a pain even in sulking

portrays.reason: Between two as blended as earth and water, a quarrel is called better than heaven.
portrays.quote: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel

portrays.reason: Sulking is the joy of desire, and its own joy is the embrace that ends it.
portrays.quote: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it

portrays.reason: She sets out to sulk, sees her heart is ready to join him and gives in.
portrays.quote: I went off meaning to sulk

portrays.reason: Her heart forgets what it came to do and goes to join him instead.
portrays.quote: my heart forgot that and went to join him

portrays.reason: A sulk is sweet only with someone who loves you, as water is sweet in the shade.
portrays.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you

answers.reason: A sulk is like salt. The right amount helps, and drawing it out spoils things.
answers.quote: Drawing it out is like a little too much

portrays.reason: She refuses him because every woman’s eyes have had their share of him.
portrays.quote: I won’t go near your chest, you philanderer

portrays.reason: Any flower he wears becomes proof, to her, of some other woman.
portrays.quote: You wear it to show some woman

portrays.reason: His “more than anyone” only makes her ask who the others are.
portrays.quote: she sulked: “Than who? Than who?”

portrays.reason: He promises not to part in this life, and she hears that he means to part in the next.
portrays.quote: her eyes filled with tears

portrays.reason: To her, “I thought of you” can only mean he had forgotten her first.
portrays.quote: So why did you forget me?

portrays.reason: She blesses his sneeze, then takes it back and weeps at who might be thinking of him.
portrays.quote: Who was thinking of you, that you sneezed

portrays.reason: When he holds back a sneeze, she weeps at what he must be hiding.
portrays.quote: Are you hiding from me

portrays.reason: His soothing her becomes proof of how he must be with others.
portrays.quote: So this is how you are with others too

portrays.reason: Even his quiet gaze is read as thinking of someone else.
portrays.quote: Who are you thinking of

portrays.reason: He can’t even tell what she is: a goddess, a peacock or a woman.
portrays.quote: My heart is lost in doubt

portrays.reason: Her answering look hits him like a goddess with an army behind her.
portrays.quote: a goddess who strikes had brought an army

portrays.reason: He says he has only now learned what death is, and it has a woman’s eyes.
portrays.quote: I never knew before what they call death

portrays.reason: One glance holds death, an eye and a doe at once, and he can’t separate them.
portrays.quote: Is it death? Is it an eye? Is it a doe?

portrays.reason: Her eyes, not hidden by her brows, leave him trembling with pain.
portrays.quote: this trembling pain

portrays.reason: The strength that enemies feared in battle breaks before a bright forehead.
portrays.quote: has broken before it

portrays.reason: She looks down when he looks, and looks at him when he doesn’t.
portrays.quote: When I look at her, she looks at the ground

portrays.reason: To him her shy look and modesty are ornament enough.
portrays.quote: the shy look of a doe

portrays.reason: Shame stops her from telling him what she can’t hide.
portrays.quote: telling the one who caused it brings me shame

portrays.reason: She can’t carry both, and begs her heart to give up one.
portrays.quote: give up desire or give up modesty

portrays.reason: Modesty is the bolt on the door, and the axe of desire breaks it down.
portrays.quote: the door of reserve, bolted with modesty

portrays.reason: Caught up with a heart that can’t forget him, she finds her modesty gone.
portrays.quote: I have forgotten even my modesty

portrays.reason: When the one she cherishes does all she longs for, modesty is forgotten.
portrays.quote: we don’t even know there is such a thing as modesty

portrays.reason: Bitterly calls the base fortunate, since they alone have no worry in their hearts.
portrays.quote: for their hearts have no worries

portrays.reason: Even in a sulk there is a worry working away: will this delay coming together?
portrays.quote: the worry over whether union will be delayed

portrays.reason: Yesterday’s want was almost too much, and the first thought today is whether it will come again.
portrays.quote: Will it come today too

portrays.reason: Sleep is possible even in a fire, but not with poverty on your mind.
portrays.quote: In poverty there is no sleep at all

answers.reason: Says the sorrow of the mind is hard to shift unless you reach the feet of the one who has no equal.
answers.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

answers.reason: Says the way to meet what is to come is to guard against it, and then nothing comes to shake you.
answers.quote: have no suffering that comes and shakes them

portrays.reason: However strong the walls, being afraid leaves you with no fort.
portrays.quote: There is no fort for those who are afraid

portrays.reason: A ruler with no defences ready takes fright when war comes, and quickly falls.
portrays.quote: will take fright when it does

portrays.reason: Size and sharp tusks don’t stop an elephant being afraid when a tiger comes.
portrays.quote: yet it fears a tiger’s attack

portrays.reason: Fear of the assembly can keep all you have learned from being said, as if you weren’t there.
portrays.quote: Those who fear the assembly

answers.reason: Some fear is wisdom. Fearing what should be feared is called the way of those who understand.
answers.quote: To fear what should be feared

answers.reason: Fear of speaking before others is met by learning well beforehand.
answers.quote: so that you can answer in an assembly without fear

portrays.reason: After a lie it is your own heart, knowing what it knows, that does the burning.
portrays.quote: your own heart will burn you

portrays.reason: No outward look helps when your own heart is sinking into a fault you know is yours.
portrays.quote: your own heart sinks into what you know is a fault

portrays.reason: What is done against what has been forbidden brings pain later, even when it works.
portrays.quote: brings pain even if it succeeds

answers.reason: Once it is done, says not to do the like again. Parimelazhagar hears “don’t go on grieving”.
answers.quote: it is good not to do the like again

answers.reason: Tending living beings and holding to compassion leaves you with no deeds that frighten your own soul.
answers.quote: no deeds that make their own soul afraid

portrays.reason: Scorn stings even when it is meant as a joke.
portrays.quote: Scorn hurts, even in fun

portrays.reason: A single word of refusal is enough to take the life out of someone who has had to beg.
portrays.quote: the life goes out of those who beg

portrays.reason: States it flatly: those with nothing are scorned and the rich are honoured.
portrays.quote: Everyone scorns those who have nothing

portrays.reason: Poverty can bring even those of good family to say what shames them.
portrays.quote: poverty brings a weakness from which shameful words are born

portrays.reason: The blame falls on her for turning pale, and no one says what he has done.
portrays.quote: No one says, “He has left her.”

portrays.reason: People laugh in front of her because they have never suffered what she has.
portrays.quote: Fools laugh in front of my eyes

answers.reason: Having nothing isn’t itself the disgrace, if you have the strength called worth.
answers.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace

answers.reason: Following those who despise you brings neither fame nor the land of the gods, so why do it?
answers.quote: why follow behind those who despise you

answers.reason: Says to hold yourself higher, not lower, when your means shrink.
answers.quote: When your means shrink, stand tall

answers.reason: Where you have been put doesn’t settle what you are. Those who aren’t low aren’t made low by it.
answers.quote: Those who aren’t low aren’t low, even sitting low

answers.reason: Gruel as thin as water, from your own labour, is called sweeter than anything.
answers.quote: nothing is sweeter than eating what your own labour has brought

answers.reason: Lacking good fortune shames no one. Disgrace lies only in knowing what must be done and making no effort.
answers.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one

portrays.reason: Regret arrives with the blow, when it is too late to guard against what could have been prevented.
portrays.quote: will regret that mistake when the blow lands

portrays.reason: Hidden wrongdoing brings trouble after trouble, until the cry comes: what have we done?
portrays.quote: until they cry “What have we done?”

portrays.reason: She agreed to his leaving, can’t bear it now, and has no one to tell.
portrays.quote: I agreed to go without the kindness

portrays.reason: Her eyes looked first and understood later, and now they suffer for it.
portrays.quote: looked without knowing what would come

answers.reason: If you have done what makes you cry out, don’t do the like again. Parimelazhagar hears “don’t go on grieving”.
answers.quote: it is good not to do the like again

portrays.reason: Living among people who aren’t your own is named as a pain, before she even gets to parting.
portrays.quote: It is painful to live in a town without your own people

portrays.reason: When everyone else sleeps, she is the only one awake.
portrays.quote: Even at midnight I alone am here

portrays.reason: All living things are asleep, and the night and she are left with each other.
portrays.quote: has no companion but me

portrays.reason: Alone with her thoughts, she finds her own heart stays only to eat at her.
portrays.quote: When I sat alone and thought

portrays.reason: Deserted even by her own heart, she asks if it is because the ruined have no friends.
portrays.quote: the ruined have no friends

answers.reason: Being alone is called better than calling your own those who fail you when it counts.
answers.quote: Better to be alone

answers.reason: Says where friendship comes from: loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and the warmth brings it.
answers.quote: that warmth brings friendship

portrays.reason: Words leave a scar that stays after a burn from fire has healed.
portrays.quote: A scar burned by the tongue never heals

portrays.reason: Being deserted in your ruin goes on burning, even when you think of it at the hour of death.
portrays.quote: desert you in your ruin burns the heart

portrays.reason: She asks what people could do as enemies, if this is the suffering they bring as friends.
portrays.quote: bring suffering even in friendship

portrays.reason: Friends whose acts and words don’t match leave a bitterness that reaches you even in a dream.
portrays.quote: bitter even in a dream

portrays.reason: A friend who doesn’t agree at heart is an anvil. When they find their chance, you are what gets struck.
portrays.quote: you are struck on it

answers.reason: Says not to take on friends who cut away your strength in trouble.
answers.quote: Don’t take the friendship of those who cut away your strength

answers.reason: Says to leave friends who don’t fit, even if it costs you something to get free.
answers.quote: leave the friendship of those who don’t fit

answers.reason: Those who are warm in private and blame you in public are to be kept away altogether.
answers.quote: come near you at all

portrays.reason: Doubting someone you have come to trust is named as a suffering that doesn’t end.
portrays.quote: to doubt someone you have come to trust

portrays.reason: Suspicion, once in place, is very hard for anyone to clear.
portrays.quote: Once suspicion has set in

portrays.reason: Even those who understand can sometimes leave, so she can’t rest on anyone’s word.
portrays.quote: It is hard to trust

portrays.reason: Living with those who aren’t of one mind with you is like sharing a hut with a snake.
portrays.quote: sharing a hut with a snake

answers.reason: Trust follows testing, and goes only as far as the testing showed.
answers.quote: After testing, trust them with what they can be trusted with

answers.reason: Look at a person’s good points and faults together, and judge by which are more.
answers.quote: see which are more, and judge them by that

answers.reason: A person’s own deeds are what to test them by.
answers.quote: their own deeds are the touchstone

portrays.reason: Names the moment itself: the thought that this is too hard.
portrays.quote: Don’t lose heart and say “This is too hard.”

answers.reason: The answer to “too hard” is effort, which gives you the greatness to finish.
answers.quote: Effort will give you greatness

answers.reason: A flood of trouble dies away once a wise person sets their mind to it.
answers.quote: Even a flood of trouble dies away

answers.reason: Those who won’t be troubled by trouble turn it back on itself.
answers.quote: will give trouble trouble

answers.reason: Keep going like an ox through every blocked place, and the trouble is what gets into trouble.
answers.quote: pulls through every blocked place

answers.reason: Stay unbroken, and even troubles that pile up are the ones in trouble.
answers.quote: Even if they come heaped one on another

answers.reason: Aiming high keeps its worth even when it falls short.
answers.quote: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing

answers.reason: Missing something great is called better than hitting something small.
answers.quote: a spear that missed an elephant

answers.reason: Struck by a mass of arrows, an elephant stands its ground, and so do the strong when things fall apart.
answers.quote: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart

answers.reason: Says to keep your mind off what makes your spirit shrink.
answers.quote: Don’t think of things that make your spirit small

answers.reason: What you have listened to becomes a prop when you falter.
answers.quote: a prop to lean on when you falter

answers.reason: Says to stay resolute in work that brings joy, even when great pain comes.
answers.quote: Even if great pain comes, be resolute

portrays.reason: People who suffer and can’t bear it have their tears, and those tears are called a weapon that wears away wealth.
portrays.quote: those who suffer and can’t bear it

portrays.reason: Whatever way round it you plan, fate is there ahead of you.
portrays.quote: Even as you plan a way around it, it gets there first

portrays.reason: She can see the sea she is in, and no raft to cross it.
portrays.quote: There is no safe raft to cross it

portrays.reason: She swims on and no shore comes into sight.
portrays.quote: and see no shore

portrays.reason: With nothing left, she asks her own heart to think of any cure at all.
portrays.quote: any cure at all for this unending sickness

answers.reason: Even where the result is denied, the effort still pays its wages.
answers.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

answers.reason: Where action isn’t possible, the next step is to look for the way that will work.
answers.quote: look for the way that will work and do that

answers.reason: Knowing the body is a target for suffering is what stops turmoil being taken as distress.
answers.quote: don’t treat the turmoil that comes on them as distress

portrays.reason: Her eyes can’t sleep when he stays away and can’t sleep when he comes.
portrays.quote: When he comes they don’t sleep

portrays.reason: Desire gives her heart no rest, keeping it at work in the dead of night.
portrays.quote: Even in the dead of night it rules my heart

portrays.reason: Her desire can’t stay still. It wanders the streets in a daze, thinking no one knows.
portrays.quote: wanders the streets in a daze

portrays.reason: Unsure of one more moment, people still run through thoughts by the ten million.
portrays.quote: they think thoughts by the ten million

portrays.reason: However little he cherished her, her eyes can’t rest without seeing him.
portrays.quote: my eyes will not rest until they see him

portrays.reason: A good person’s poverty is this: not being able to settle when they can’t do what they must.
portrays.quote: being unable to rest when they can’t do what they must

answers.reason: Understanding is what stops the mind going wherever it goes, and turns it from evil to good.
answers.quote: doesn’t let the mind go wherever it goes

portrays.reason: Great delight can bring a carelessness called worse than boundless rage.
portrays.quote: the high spirits of great delight

portrays.reason: Names the moment when delight starts to feel like strength.
portrays.quote: When your delight makes you feel strong

portrays.reason: A fool with something of their own in hand is compared to a madman getting drunk.
portrays.quote: like a madman getting drunk

answers.reason: At the height of delight, the thing to do is call to mind those neglect has ruined.
answers.quote: remember those who were ruined by neglect

antidotes.reason: Holding back anger is named with restraint as what brings righteousness to you.
antidotes.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint

antidotes.reason: Anger is one of four things that righteousness is defined as being free of.
antidotes.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four

antidotes.reason: Keeping the heart free of envy is itself to be taken as the rule of conduct.
antidotes.quote: Make it your rule of conduct

antidotes.reason: Envy heads the list of four things that righteousness is a life free of.
antidotes.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four

antidotes.reason: Letting go is set against pain, thing by thing. What you have let go of can’t hurt you.
antidotes.quote: you suffer no more pain

antidotes.reason: Reaching the Lord’s feet is what the opening chapter sets against suffering and the sorrow of the mind.
antidotes.quote: will have no suffering, ever

antidotes.reason: Holding to compassion is set against misery, with the earth itself called as witness.
antidotes.quote: Those who hold to compassion have no misery

antidotes.reason: Friendship is defined by what it does with pain: it shares it when ruin comes and takes trouble away at once.
antidotes.quote: shares the pain when ruin comes

antidotes.reason: Wanting nothing is set above all wealth, against the craving that is never filled.
antidotes.quote: no great wealth here to match wanting nothing

antidotes.reason: Fearing craving is called righteousness, and craving is one of four things righteousness is free of.
antidotes.quote: To fear it is righteousness

antidotes.reason: Renouncing completely is set against being caught in the net of those who hold on.
antidotes.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived

antidotes.reason: Attachment to the one with no attachment is the one hold offered for letting go of all others.
antidotes.quote: Hold to the attachment of the one who has no attachment

antidotes.reason: Knowing what to rest on, in the chapter on truth, is what lets attachment die.
antidotes.quote: live so that attachment dies

antidotes.reason: The feet of the one who has no equal are named as what removes the sorrow of the mind.
antidotes.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

antidotes.reason: Guarding against what is to come is set against the suffering that comes and shakes you.
antidotes.quote: guard against what is to come

antidotes.reason: Learning is set against fear of the assembly: learn well so that you can answer without fear.
antidotes.quote: Learn by the right path

antidotes.reason: Holding to compassion is what leaves a person with no deeds their own soul fears.
antidotes.quote: no deeds that make their own soul afraid

antidotes.reason: Worth is named as the strength that keeps having nothing from being a disgrace.
antidotes.quote: the strength called worth

antidotes.reason: Keeping your actions clean is what spares you the cry of “What have I done?”
antidotes.quote: Don’t do what will make you cry

antidotes.reason: Testing is set against doubt: trusting the untested and doubting the tested both bring suffering.
antidotes.quote: Trust no one without testing them

antidotes.reason: Chapter 63 sets staying unbroken against trouble: heaped troubles that reach such a person are themselves in trouble.
antidotes.quote: the troubles that reach an unbroken person are themselves in trouble

antidotes.reason: Effort is the answer given to the thought that something is too hard.
antidotes.quote: Effort will give you greatness

antidotes.reason: Thinking of rising higher is said to keep its worth even when it fails.
antidotes.quote: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

antidotes.reason: Listening is named as the prop that holds you up when you falter.
antidotes.quote: a prop to lean on when you falter

antidotes.reason: Effort is set against fate itself: even where god won’t allow the result, it pays its wages.
antidotes.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

antidotes.reason: Remembering those ruined by neglect is what keeps delight from turning into carelessness.
antidotes.quote: remember those who were ruined by neglect
